endorsements.name: Mickey "@HackingThings" Shkatov
endorsements.label: Bring Your Own Root Of Trust
endorsements.description: Modern computers depend on a hardware root of trust: a component assumed to start trustworthy and is used to verify everything that follows. This has evolved from ROM boot code and fixed keys into TPMs, secure boot chains, external security controllers, and attestation mechanisms used far beyond disk encryption. Today, platforms trust these devices because they are certified, immutable, and built into the hardware, but what if that assumption is wrong? Starting from real hardware traces, failed approaches, and a pile of development boards, we arrive at a $45 FPGA-based SPI TPM that can appear to Windows 11 as a platform trust anchor. From there, we explore what this means for secure boot, measured boot, platform attestation, anticheat, AI infrastructure, and the broader belief that hardware identity is difficult to counterfeit. We will release the code, gateware, prompts, and data so others can reproduce the work and push it further.
